question.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=3-\frac{4}{\sqrt[3]{x}}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=3-\frac{4}{\sqrt[3]{x}}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=3-\frac{4}{\sqrt[3]{y}}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =3-\frac{4}{\sqrt[3]{y}} \\ x-3 & =-\frac{4}{\sqrt[3]{y}} \\ 3-x & =\frac{4}{\sqrt[3]{y}} \\ \frac{1}{3-x} & =\frac{\sqrt[3]{y}}{4} \\ \sqrt[3]{y} & =\frac{4}{3-x} \\ (\sqrt[3]{y})^{3} & ={(\frac{4}{3-x})}^{3} \\ y & =\frac{64}{(3-x)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{64}{(3-x)^{3}}.
$$

**Note**: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are

$$
x\ne 0,\,f(x)\ne 3.
$$

Therefore, the domain and range of ${f}^{-1}(x)$ are

$$
x\ne 3,\,{f}^{-1}(x)\ne 0.
$$
